To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the eigenvalue distributions of the Dirac operator in the continuum limit are in agreement with Random Matrix Theory predictions for the first nontrivial eigenvalue, that the eigenvalue distribution of the first nontrival eigenvalue in the lattice Dirac operator agrees with the prediction of Random Matrix Theory for the first non-trivial eigenvalue, and that the agreement of the lattice and continuum Dirac operator spectra is achieved for volumes larger than about 1.2 fm4.

the distribution of the first non-zero Dirac operator eigenvalue is given by the chiral Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE) if the lattice volume exceeds about ( 1.2 fm )4, while the distributions of the higher eigenvalues are given by the chGUE if the volume exceeds a few times ( 1.5 fm )4.
(i) Random matrix theory (RMT) is an accurate description of the spectra of the overlap operator for quenched QCD on a lattice with spacing 0.05 fm and a volume of about (1.5 fm)3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spectra of the Dirac operator, and the application of Random Matrix theory to the spectra of the overlap fermion Dirac operator.
a detailed study of the spectra of the QCD Dirac operator in a finite Euclidean space-time volume.
the use of random matrix theory to predict the spectra of the Dirac operator in QCD and the use of those predictions in order to determine the topological charge of the vacuum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the predictions of Random Matrix Theory are valid at the level of the lowest eigenvalue in QCD with a large volume and a small number of flavours.
the RMT predictions are valid for the first non-trivial eigenvalue in quenched Qcd with overlap fermions at β=5.2 and 5.6, and for the lowest 10-20 eigenvalues in the chiral limit.
the eigenvalue distributions in the spectrum of the overlap Dirac operator are consistent with the predictions of Random Matrix Theory for a chiral unitary ensemble.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Random Matrix Theory is a powerful tool to understand the low-energy properties of QCD.
we found that the eigenvalue distributions of the Dirac operator are universal, i.e. independent of the gauge ensemble and the quark mass, as long as the quark mass is not too small.

the eigenvalue distribution of a massless Dirac operator is universal in the sense that it does not depend on the details of the gauge field ensemble, and that this distribution is described by Random Matrix Theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Random Matrix Theory provides a powerful tool for the analysis of the low-lying Dirac operator spectrum.
Random Matrix Theory can be used to predict the eigenvalue distributions of the Dirac operator in QCD.
